#Question 1

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

NYC_transit_df =
  read_csv("./NYC_Transit_Subway_Entrance_And_Exit_Data.csv",
           na = c ("NA", ".", ""))|>
janitor::clean_names() |>
  select(line, station_name, station_latitude, station_longitude, route1:route11, entry, vending, entrance_type, ada) |>
mutate(
  entry = 
         case_match(
           entry,
           "YES" ~ TRUE,
           "NO" ~ FALSE
         ))
  
```
This data set contains information on the entrances and exits for each station in NYC. It contains `r ncol(NYC_transit_df)` variables. From the original data, I cleaned the names, and kept only the variables of interest using the select line followed by the variable names. Then I converted the entry variable from a character (Yes vs No), to a logical variable. The final dataset has `r nrow(NYC_transit_df)` rows and `r ncol(NYC_transit_df)` columns. The data is not tidy because the Route variable is spread across 11 variable columns from route1:route11.
